title: refactor: migrate monolithic presubmit to language-aware CI orchestrator with dep-minimizer
author: Priya Menon
description:
Problem: our current presubmit runner is a monolithic bash/python combo that schedules lint and test jobs by coarse repo paths. This causes redundant work (same linters run across many subpackages), long feedback loops for language-specific changes, and brittle ad-hoc dependency bootstrapping.

Goal: introduce a language-aware CI orchestrator (Go) that: (1) inspects changed files and constructs a minimal presubmit plan per-language, (2) delegates to existing language runner plugins (py, ts, go, docker), (3) integrates the dependency-minimizer (dep-minimizer) to skip unnecessary package installs, and (4) exposes a dry-run preflight mode for release automation. The change should reduce CI runtime for common PRs and make presubmit behavior predictable.

What this PR does (summary):
- Add a go-based orchestrator cmd/ci/orchestrator that computes a language-aware presubmit graph and emits a compact job manifest.
- Replace the single presubmit.sh entrypoint with orchestrator invocations in .github/workflows/presubmit.yml while keeping backwards compatibility flags for local dev.
- Add dep-minimizer integration: the orchestrator asks dep-minimizer for a minimal dependency snapshot per job (uses existing lockfiles; no new lockfile format).
- Introduce a --dry-run=preflight mode used by release automation to validate staged releases without full artifact builds.
- Add lightweight telemetry events (ci.plan_size, ci.job_estimate_ms) and coarse retry/backoff knobs for flaky integration shards.
- Update docs: docs/dev/ci-orchestrator.md and quickstart snippets in devcontainers.

Checklist:
- [x] Architect review and design doc (Linear ENG-2534 attached in description)
- [x] Implement orchestrator + plugins with unit tests
- [x] Migrate presubmit workflow; keep feature flag for 2 weeks rollout
- [x] Add release preflight dry-run hook and document usage
- [x] Monitor CI impact via one-week canary

Commits (high-level):
- 7efb1ac add go orchestrator scaffolding and basic language detector
- a1d4c2b implement dep-minimizer client + caching layer for job snapshots
- 34b7e9a refactor: replace presubmit.sh with orchestrator invocation in workflow
- d2c9efa tests: add unit tests for plan generator and plugin interface
- b5f8d22 docs: add dev guide and dry-run examples

Files changed (high-level):
- cmd/ci/orchestrator/main.go (new)
- internal/ci/plan.go (new)
- tools/dep-minimizer/client.go (new)
- .github/workflows/presubmit.yml (modified)
- scripts/presubmit.sh (deprecated - wrapper kept for local)
- docs/dev/ci-orchestrator.md (new)
- go.mod / go.sum (adds new deps: cobra, semver, prometheus-client)

Why this is safe to roll out incrementally:
- The workflow change is gated by a repository-level feature flag CI_ORCHESTRATOR_ENABLED. The default remains off for two weeks while the canary team (engineers listed below) validates results. The old presubmit wrapper remains and can be re-enabled by unsetting the flag.

Metrics we will track (post-merge):
- median presubmit latency by change size (goal: -25% for small changes)
- CI compute minutes used per PR (goal: -20% for typical docs/TS changes)
- false-negative presubmit failures vs. monolith baseline (goal: <= 1%)

Related Linear tickets: ENG-2534, ENG-2598, PM-388

Notes on compatibility and tradeoffs:
- The orchestrator relies on existing language runner plugins rather than reimplementing linters/test harnesses; this keeps behavior stable.
- Dep-minimizer is conservative by default; it will only trim installs when lockfiles are unchanged. We added a cache to avoid repeated resolution overhead.
- The Go orchestrator adds a small binary to CI images; image size increased ~4MB. We measured no measurable cold-start impact on ephemeral runners.

Testing and CI: unit tests run locally via go test and we have an integration workflow presubmit-canary that exercises the orchestrator with a sampled subset of PRs. During the first run one flaky integration shard failed (npm-install on windows-late) and was retriggered; see review thread.
